text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) raised its main interest rate to a historic high of 300 percent annually from 108 percent in a move to relieve pressure on the slumping national currency, the lev, on the local forex market.
This is the fifth rate hike since the beginning of the year, when the key interest rate was 34 precent. @
-- The BNB placed nine commercial banks under a special supervision in a bid to restore financial stability through rehabilitation and restucturing of the country's ailing banking system.
-- The cabinet is expected to raise the maximum fuel prices for October by an average of 20 percent above current levels due to the fall of the lev against the dollar, officials said.
-- Bulgaria signed a contract for the sale of 67 percent of Sheraton Sofia Hotel Balkan to the South Korea's giant Daewoo Corp for $22.3 million due to be paid in cash, Privatisation Agency said.
-- Russia's gas giant Gasprom decided to acquire a 34-percent stake in Bulgaria's Credit Bank, part of the country's biggest private conglomerate Multigroup, the bank's head Evgeni Goranov said.
-- Macedonia's exports to Bulgaria fell by 88.6 percent in the first half of the year, Macedonia's statistics office said.
-- Bulgaria's two biggest trade unions said they would seek the resignation of Zhan Videnov's Socialist cabinet over its inability to cope with the country's acute economic crisis. @

-- Bulgaria's former premier Reneta Indzova said she would appeal to the Supreme Court against a refusal by the Central Electoral Committee to register her as a independent candidate for the country's presidential elections due on October 27.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose to 71.8 billion levs on September 17 or 88.96 of the planned for the whole year, the finance ministry said.

-- Individuals' deposits in banks, against which the BNB opens insolvency suits would be guaranteed 100 percent but would be paid only after the court declares the banks bankrupt, under draft amendments to the deposit guarantee law approved by the cabinet.
So far depositors can draw their savings in banks slated for closure as soon as the BNB files insolvency suits against them.

-- Bulgaria's Supreme Court began deliberations on a plea of the First Private Bank against the Bulgarian National Bank over the BNB's decision from May this year to place the debt-ridden bank under a special supervision.
A court ruling could be expected two weeks.
